description:
One standing behavioural suite asserts that each of the five campaign backends computes the same permanents as the generic reference routine, so no execution path certifies its own correctness privately.

## Background

This leaf lands last in the execution layer, which is what lets it exist: the five backends the campaign can select — scalar, batch-parallel, intra-matrix, generic Ryser, and accelerator — exists by then, so one suite can assert they agree rather than each path asserting its own correctness in its own tests. That is what `@/inv/backend-behavioral-equivalence` asks for and what a one-off equivalence run does not provide.

The suite is a standing test rather than a script, because the property it guards — per-matrix agreement across paths — must keep holding as the paths evolve, and a script that was run once proves nothing about the tree as it stands.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One shared behavioural suite asserts per-matrix agreement across the five campaign backends — scalar, batch-parallel, intra-matrix, generic Ryser, and accelerator — against the generic reference routine on a common matrix set for each supported field.
- [hard] REQ-02: The suite runs as a standing test rather than a one-off script, with accelerator cases skipped and reported as skipped on hosts without the device.
- [hard] REQ-03: The common matrix set is drawn through a fixed seed recorded in the test, so a failure reproduces from the test alone.

## Notes

The backend set the suite covers is the campaign-selectable set as the execution layer defines it; a backend added later joins the suite in the change that adds it, which is what keeps the suite the single certification point.
title: Shared behavioural conformance suite across campaign backends
